lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Which conclusion is stronger: "The library is better now" or "The library has more services than in 1990, because the librarian and two photos show new rooms"?

FEEDBACK
The second, because it answers the question with named evidence. The first is an opinion with no evidence.

WATCH FOR
A conclusion that overclaims, such as saying something happened everywhere from one source, is not supported by the evidence.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Example conclusion: "The library has changed since 1990 mainly by adding services. Evidence: two photos show a new computer room and the librarian said the children's section opened in 1998. A limit is that we only had two photos, so we cannot say when each change happened."

TRY FIRST
Which conclusion is stronger: "The library is better now" or "The library has more services than in 1990, because the librarian and two photos show new rooms"?

FEEDBACK
The second, because it answers the question with named evidence. The first is an opinion with no evidence.
teach_steps.explain:
A conclusion answers the inquiry question using evidence. It names the strongest evidence, states how sure you are and explains the limits, such as too few sources. A good conclusion can also suggest a new question.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner base claims on sources, places and respectful community knowledge, rather than guessing from a single picture. Keep every claim linked to evidence.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the sources, map features or community examples that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your record with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your evidence? If a detail is uncertain, identify what source you would need next. One deliberate, evidence-based revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
teach_steps.notice: A conclusion that overclaims, such as saying something happened everywhere from one source, is not supported by the evidence. Correct the claim or use of sources, not just the neatness of the poster.
